newsitem.title: USA: Tropical depression better organized, could grow.
newsitem.headline: Tropical depression better organized, could grow.

text.p: The 10th tropical depression of the Atlantic hurricane season was becoming better organized as it moved slowly through the Gulf of Mexico on Sunday and could soon become a tropical storm, the National Hurricane Center said.
At 5 p.m. EDT (2100 GMT) the center of the depression was near latitude 25.1 north and longitude 91.6 west or about 350 miles (560 km) south-southwest of New Orleans.
It was moving east near ten mph (16 kph) and was expected to take an east-northeastward track during the next 24 hours, forecasters said.

Maximum sustained winds were 35 mph (55 kph) and the depression would likely become a tropical storm later Sunday, forecasters said. A tropical storm watch was expected for a portion of the northeast Gulf coast by early Monday.
Tropical depressions become tropical storms and are given names when maximum winds reach 39 mph (62 kph) and gain hurricane status when winds hit 74 mph (119 kph).
The depression would be named Josephine if it strengthened into a tropical storm.
